lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Ephesians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the saints at Ephesus: God's blessings in Christ, salvation by grace, the unity of Jew and Gentile in one body, and how to walk worthy in the church, home and spiritual battle (1:1-6:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Ephesians and say what its two halves are about?
ev: Describe the two halves: what God has done in Christ (1-3) and how to walk worthy (4-6)

nodes.t: Blessed in Christ: chosen, adopted, redeemed, sealed
nodes.d: Paul blesses God, who in Christ chose us before the foundation of the world, adopted us, redeemed us through his blood, made known the mystery of his will, and sealed believers with the Holy Spirit as the pledge of the inheritance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God has done for believers in Christ, using Ephesians 1:3-14?
ev: List the blessings Paul names in 1:3-14
Say when God chose us and for what purpose (1:4)
Say what the Holy Spirit is for believers (1:13-14)

nodes.t: Paul's prayer: Christ above all, head of the church
nodes.d: Paul gives thanks and prays that the Ephesians may know the hope of God's calling and the greatness of his power, which raised Christ and set him far above every power as head over all things to the church, his body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about Christ's position and the church in Ephesians 1:20-23?
ev: Say what Paul prays that they may know (1:17-19)
Describe where God has set Christ (1:20-22)
Say what the church is to Christ (1:22-23)

nodes.t: Dead in sin, saved by grace through faith
nodes.d: Paul says that Christians were dead in trespasses and followed the world, the devil and the flesh, but God, rich in mercy, made them alive with Christ; salvation is by grace through faith, not by works, and believers are created for good works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Ephesians 2:8-10 says a person is saved and what follows from it?
ev: Describe the condition before salvation (2:1-3)
Explain 2:8-9
Say what we were created in Christ for (2:10)

nodes.t: One new man: Jew and Gentile reconciled
nodes.d: Paul says Gentiles were once far from Israel and the covenants of promise, but are brought near by the blood of Christ, who broke down the dividing wall, made both one and gave both access to the Father; together they are built into a holy temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Christ made Jew and Gentile one, using Ephesians 2:13-18?
ev: Describe the Gentiles' former state (2:11-12)
Say what Christ did to the dividing wall (2:14-16)
Explain the picture of the household and temple (2:19-22)

nodes.t: The mystery of Christ and Paul's second prayer
nodes.d: Paul explains the mystery made known to him, that Gentiles are fellow heirs of the same body and of the promise in Christ, that the church shows God's wisdom to the powers, and prays that they know the love of Christ and be filled with the fulness of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state the mystery Paul describes in Ephesians 3:6 and what he prays for in 3:16-19?
ev: State the mystery of 3:6
Say what the church makes known (3:10)
Summarise Paul's prayer in 3:16-19
Say who receives glory in 3:20-21

nodes.t: Unity of the body and gifts for building up
nodes.d: Paul urges the Ephesians to walk worthy and keep the unity of the Spirit, lists the "one" things of the faith, and says the ascended Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers to equip the saints and build up the body until it is mature.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Christ gave pastors and teachers to the church, using Ephesians 4:11-16?
ev: List the sevenfold unity of 4:4-6
Name the gifts given in 4:11
Say what the gifts are for (4:12-16)

nodes.t: Put off the old man, put on the new
nodes.d: Paul tells the Ephesians not to live as the Gentiles do but to put off the old man and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness, with specific commands about truth, anger, work, speech and forgiveness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to put off the old man and put on the new, using Ephesians 4:22-24 and one example from 4:25-32?
ev: Contrast the old and new man (4:22-24)
List specific commands in 4:25-32
Say what we are told not to grieve (4:30)

nodes.t: Walk in love, light and wisdom
nodes.d: Paul tells the Ephesians to walk in love as Christ loved us, to avoid immorality and covetousness, to walk as children of light and not be drunk with wine but filled with the Spirit, and to submit to one another.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what walking as a child of light means, using Ephesians 5:8-11?
ev: Say how we are to walk (5:2, 5:8, 5:15)
Contrast drunkenness and being filled with the Spirit (5:18)
Say what follows from being filled (5:19-21)

nodes.t: Marriage and Christ and the church
nodes.d: Paul instructs wives and husbands, grounding the husband's love and the wife's submission in the relation of Christ to the church, quotes the scripture about two becoming one flesh, and calls this a great mystery concerning Christ and the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul connects marriage with Christ and the church in Ephesians 5:22-33?
ev: Say what Paul commands wives and husbands (5:22, 5:25)
Describe what Christ did for the church (5:25-27)
Say what Paul says the "great mystery" is about (5:32)

nodes.t: Children, parents, servants and masters
nodes.d: Paul tells children to obey their parents in the Lord, quotes the commandment to honour father and mother, tells fathers to bring children up in the Lord, and gives instructions to servants and masters who both answer to a Master in heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells children and parents in Ephesians 6:1-4?
ev: Quote the commandment Paul cites (6:2)
Say what fathers are told (6:4)
Say what masters are reminded of (6:9)

nodes.t: The whole armour of God
nodes.d: Paul calls believers to be strong in the Lord and put on the armour of God to stand against the devil and spiritual powers, listing truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation and the word of God, with prayer, and asks for prayer for himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the armour of God in Ephesians 6:14-17 and say what each piece stands for in the text?
ev: Say who we wrestle against (6:12)
List the pieces of armour (6:14-17)
Explain the role of prayer (6:18-20)

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: The garden of Eden
nodes.d: God plants a garden, places the man in it with a command, and forms the woman as a helper fit for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the garden and the one thing God told the man not to do?
ev: Retell the formation of the man and the woman
State God's command about the tree (2:16-17)

nodes.t: Exodus: overview
nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.t: The Ten Commandments
nodes.d: God speaks all these words, beginning by saying he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt. They cover having no other gods, no images, not taking his name in vain, remembering the sabbath, honouring father and mother, and not killing, committing adultery, stealing, bearing false witness or coveting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the Ten Commandments in order and say what comes before them in 20:2?
ev: Recite the ten commandments in order from the Bible
Say what 20:2 says before the commandments begin
Say the reason given for the sabbath (20:11)

nodes.t: Psalms: overview
nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 8: what is man? the LORD’s majesty and man’s place
nodes.d: The speaker praises the LORD’s excellent name, considers the heavens, the moon and stars, and asks what man is that God remembers him, saying God made him a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory, with dominion over the works of his hands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 8:3-6 and say what it teaches about God and man?
ev: Read 8:3-8 and list what is put under man’s dominion.

nodes.t: Psalm 68: let God arise
nodes.d: The psalm begins with Let God arise and his enemies be scattered, calls God a father of the fatherless and judge of the widows who leads his people, and calls the kingdoms of the earth to sing to God who rides on the heavens.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 68:5-6 says about God’s care for the weak?
ev: Read 68:1-6 and 68:32-35 and note who is called to rejoice and sing.

nodes.t: Zechariah: overview
nodes.d: Zechariah, prophet in the second year of Darius, receives a call to return, eight night visions about Jerusalem, Joshua and Zerubbabel, answers about fasting and promises for Zion, and two later burdens about the shepherd, the pierced one and the day of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Zechariah as visions, a question about fasting and two later burdens?
ev: Say that chapters 1-6 are visions and 7-8 answer a question about fasting
Name the two 'burdens' of 9-11 and 12-14 (9:1, 12:1)

nodes.t: The LORD returns to dwell in Jerusalem
nodes.d: The LORD says he has returned to Zion and Jerusalem will be a city of truth with old people and playing children in her streets; he will save his people, make them a blessing, and tells them to speak truth and judge truly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Zechariah 8:1-17 pictures Jerusalem when the LORD returns?
ev: Describe the picture of 8:4-5
Read the promise of 8:8
List the commands of 8:16-17
